title: Use cases to entities
idea: Requirement analysis turns a loose brief into use cases, who does what, and entities, the nouns that hold data and rules, before any class is drawn.
points: A use case names an actor, a goal and the result the system returns.
Nouns in the requirements become candidate entities; verbs become service methods.
Constraints such as capacity or valid hours become checks inside the entity.
Ask about unclear rules early: back-to-back slots, time zones, who may cancel.

parts.label: Actor
parts.note: Becomes the Employee entity and the caller of the use case.

parts.label: Use case
parts.note: A verb, so it becomes a service method: BookingService.book.

parts.label: Rule
parts.note: Free means no overlapping booking; the ConflictPolicy decides that.

parts.label: Constraint
parts.note: Search filters by capacity; a Room must seat at least one person.

parts.label: Value
parts.note: A slot stored as hours, 10.0 to 11.5. The end must come after the start.

parts.label: Side effect
parts.note: Something reacts after the booking is saved: the NotificationService.

code.title: Entities with invariants
code.caption: Four entities as records. The rules from the brief live in their constructors.

walk.text: `Building` and `Employee` are plain data for now: an id and a name.
The compact constructor guards capacity, so no room can seat zero people.
`Booking` rejects slots outside the day or ending before they start.
Entities refer to each other by id, not by holding whole objects.
Bad input fails at construction, so invalid state never enters the system.

pitfalls: Do not make every noun a class; attendees can start as a list of ids.
Put invariants in constructors, not in callers that may forget to check them.
Settle edge rules early: does 10:00 to 11:00 clash with 11:00 to 12:00?

quiz.why: `end <= start` holds for 9 and 9, so the compact constructor throws. The `double` fields print as `9.0` in the message.

takeaway: Use cases give methods, nouns give entities, rules become constructor checks.

starters: How do I find the use cases in a vague interview prompt?
Should Booking hold a Room object or just the room id?
Why use records for entities here instead of normal classes?
